title: Service both fork oil chambers, seals and bushings
completeness: Assembled-bike fork removal, both stock oil-chamber service, outer dust/oil seals and bushings renewal, individual disturbed external O-ring renewal, cartridge bleeding/overflow verification, and wheel/brake/fork refit. Original base-valve and damper internals remain intact; no shim-stack changes or cartridge rod-seal overhaul.

source.review_note: Independent root review approved exact2024 instructions, diagrams, values and bounded scope; plain page references and stage-specific lubricant materials corrected before freeze.

applicability.included: Exact standard US 2024 YZ450F/YZ450FS with original spring forks

required_tools.name: Stable maintenance stand and secure support
required_tools.purpose: Front wheel suspended; fork legs separately supported during clamp release

required_tools.name: Suitable torque wrenches and sockets
required_tools.range_required: Accurate at applicable values from 7 to 115 N·m; account for effective lever length when using an offset adapter rather than guessing a wrench setting
required_tools.size: Accurate at7–115 N·m, plus separate precision driver accurate at0.6 N·m; account for offset-adapter lever length

required_tools.name: Metric depth/height measuring tool
required_tools.purpose: 7 mm fork projection referenced to source diagram

required_tools.name: Caliper sling/support and pad separator
required_tools.purpose: Support closed hydraulic assembly; prevent accidental pad closure while disc is absent

required_tools.name: Clean parts tray and setup log
required_tools.purpose: Preserve side-specific collars and original settings

required_tools.name: Dial gauge and suitable measuring support
Oil-level measuring/suction tool and accurate graduated volume measure
Seal-entry protective vinyl film, clean drain containers, lint-free cloths

materials.name: Lithium-soap-based grease
materials.purpose: Fork seal lips and inner-tube surface during dust-seal installation, plus axle/wheel oil-seal lips. Use fork oil on the tube during the earlier oil-seal insertion stage, as each step specifies.

required_parts.name: New piston metal / inner-tube bushing
required_parts.purpose: One per leg, PDF163 item8 and PDF169 groove.

required_parts.name: New slide metal
required_parts.purpose: One per leg, PDF163 item10 and PDF169 driver sequence.

required_parts.name: New oil seal
required_parts.purpose: One per leg, PDF163 item12; numbered face downward.

required_parts.name: New dust seal
required_parts.purpose: One per leg, PDF163 item4; no separate scraper in this source stack.

required_parts.name: New copper washer
required_parts.purpose: One per leg, PDF171 item2 at lower adjuster.

required_parts.name: New matching external damper-assembly O-ring
required_parts.purpose: One per leg at original lower cartridge groove; PDF166 top-left.

required_parts.name: New matching lower-adjuster O-ring
required_parts.purpose: One per leg at original groove; PDF166 adjuster close-up.

required_parts.name: New matching base-valve external O-rings
required_parts.purpose: Individually identify every disturbed NEW-marked position in PDF163/166; no kit contents assumed.

required_parts.name: Yamaha Suspension Oil S1
required_parts.purpose: Separate216 cm3 cartridge and270 cm3 outer fills per leg; enough for repeat bleed cycles.

required_parts.name: Lithium-soap-based grease
required_parts.purpose: Seal lips, indicated tube region and wheel/axle refit.

required_parts.name: LOCTITE locking agent
required_parts.purpose: Lower adjuster-to-inner-tube thread; source does not name grade/cure time. Record product and follow its instructions.

prerequisites: Exact original 2024 stock fork configuration; no earlier unfinished internal job or unknown assembly state.
Ability to identify the 7 mm projection reference in PDF162/173 and execute the illustrated cartridge seating technique.
Working front brake, serviceable original valve/damper internals and secure supports; damaged assemblies require separate replacement work.
critical_stop_conditions: Bent/damaged tube, worn base valve or damaged damper needing separate component replacement.
Damper does not fully extend or moves roughly after the prescribed bleed/purge.
Seal ring cannot seat, tube binds, or adjuster gap is outside specification.

settings.projection_reference: Dimension a from upper-bracket top to outer-tube top edge in PDF162/173, excluding cap/knob.
settings.restore_damping: Recorded pre-removal settings; no new tuning target.

steps.title: Record and support
steps.instruction: Record left/right rebound and compression settings and the existing fork height. This procedure returns the forks to the OEM standard 7 mm projection. Put the bike securely on its maintenance stand with the front wheel off the ground.
verification: Bike stable; original setup recorded; standard-height target understood.
steps.origin: Original illustrated companion reconciled against exact 2024 BHR source; logging/support and closed-caliper retention are explicit workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Free the hose guides
steps.instruction: Remove the number-plate bolt, release the brake hose from its upper/lower guides, then pull the plate projection free of the front fender. Keep the hose routed and unstressed.
verification: Plate removed; guide routing recorded.
steps.origin: Original illustrated companion reconciled against exact 2024 BHR source; logging/support and closed-caliper retention are explicit workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Remove the front wheel
steps.instruction: Loosen all four axle pinch bolts. Support the wheel; remove the axle nut and axle, then lower the wheel clear. Label and retain its left and right collars. Prevent the brake lever being operated with the disc absent.
verification: Wheel/axle/collars retained with correct sides; pads not forced closed.
steps.origin: Original illustrated companion reconciled against exact 2024 BHR source; logging/support and closed-caliper retention are explicit workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Support the brake assembly
steps.instruction: Remove the two caliper mounting bolts and support the complete caliper so its weight cannot pull on the hose. Keep the hose union, bleed screw, pad pin and pads undisturbed. Release the brake-hose holder from the fork protector, preserving its orientation and paint-mark position.
verification: Caliper supported; closed hydraulic circuit; hose not loaded.
steps.origin: Original illustrated companion reconciled against exact 2024 BHR source; logging/support and closed-caliper retention are explicit workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Remove the protectors
steps.instruction: Remove the three protector bolts on each fork leg and lift the protectors away. Keep the hardware grouped by side.
verification: Both protectors removed; hardware accounted for.
steps.origin: Original illustrated companion reconciled against exact 2024 BHR source; logging/support and closed-caliper retention are explicit workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Release each fork leg
steps.instruction: Support one fork leg. Loosen its upper-clamp pinch bolts, then use the specified ring wrench to loosen—but not remove—the damper assembly at the top while the lower clamp still holds the leg. Loosen the lower-clamp pinch bolts and slide the supported leg down and out. Repeat on the other side; keep each assembly upright until its internal-service steps.
verification: Both legs supported and removed; caps only loosened; no oil drained or internal components removed.
steps.origin: Original illustrated companion reconciled against exact 2024 BHR source; logging/support and closed-caliper retention are explicit workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Left fork: open and drain the outer chamber
steps.instruction: Keep parts identified by side. Unscrew the already-loosened damper assembly from the outer tube and drain the outer fork oil into a suitable container. Preserve the spring, upper spring seat and adjusting rod as each is freed; use the exploded view to maintain their order.
verification: left: Outer oil drained; left/right parts remain separate.
steps.origin: Original illustrated companion reconciled against exact 2024 BHR source; logging/support and closed-caliper retention are explicit workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Left fork: detach the lower adjuster
steps.instruction: Loosen the lower adjuster from the inner tube. Compress the inner tube and support the exposed rod locknut with the cap-bolt ring wrench positioned between tube and locknut as illustrated. Hold the locknut while unscrewing the adjuster from the rod. Retain the adjusting rod and old sealing washer for identification. Never remove the rod locknut: the rod can disappear into the cartridge.
verification: left: Adjuster detached with locknut retained; rod supported; old washer identified.
steps.origin: Original illustrated companion reconciled against exact 2024 BHR source; logging/support and closed-caliper retention are explicit workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Left fork: remove cartridge and spring
steps.instruction: With the lower adjuster detached, release the supported spring load under control and withdraw the damper assembly, upper spring seat and fork spring. Keep the spring seat orientation identified. Keep the damper-rod locknut installed.
verification: left: Damper/spring/seat removed and identified; locknut remains installed.
steps.origin: Original illustrated companion reconciled against exact 2024 BHR source; logging/support and closed-caliper retention are explicit workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Left fork: separate the fork tubes
steps.instruction: Carefully lift the dust seal and remove the stopper ring without scratching the inner tube. Slowly push the inner tube almost to bottom, then pull it back quickly as illustrated; repeat until the tubes separate. Remove the old piston metal, slide metal, oil seal and dust seal. Retain the reusable washer, stopper ring and protector guide in order. This exact-year stack has no separate scraper.
verification: left: Tubes separated without damage; renewal items separated from reusable hardware.
steps.origin: Original illustrated companion reconciled against exact 2024 BHR source; logging/support and closed-caliper retention are explicit workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Left fork: open the damper oil chamber
steps.instruction: Record the compression setting if not already recorded, then fully loosen that damping adjuster. Remove the adjuster knob and base valve while holding the cartridge with ring wrench 90890-01501 and using cap wrench 90890-01911. Drain the damper oil. Keep the base-valve assembly intact; this operation does not dismantle shim stacks or pressure-spring internals.
verification: left: Compression control fully loosened; cartridge drained; valve assembly intact.
steps.origin: Original illustrated companion reconciled against exact 2024 BHR source; logging/support and closed-caliper retention are explicit workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Left fork: inspect tubes, spring and damper
steps.instruction: Check the inner tube, oil-lock piece, outer tube and damper for damage. Measure inner-tube bend with a dial gauge: bending is half the total reading and must not exceed 0.2 mm. The fork-spring free-length limit is 492.0 mm. Record both measurements. A bent tube, damaged oil-lock piece, worn outer tube or damaged damper needs replacement; do not straighten a bent tube.
verification: left: Bend and spring length recorded; damaged/out-of-limit components replaced before assembly.
steps.origin: Original illustrated companion reconciled against exact 2024 BHR source; logging/support and closed-caliper retention are explicit workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Left fork: renew the disturbed seals
steps.instruction: Clean components and inspect the base valve, its spring/bushing, bleed screw, upper spring-seat contact face and adjuster. Failed valve/damper internals need separate component replacement; do not alter them within this service. Renew each disturbed NEW-marked external O-ring at its exact original groove using PDF 163 and PDF 166. Match each replacement before removing the next old seal and record each location. Keep the bleed screw, pressure spring and valve stacks assembled; no gas-charge work is included.
verification: left: Each disturbed seal matched to its illustrated location and renewed; all assemblies clean and serviceable.
steps.origin: Original illustrated companion reconciled against exact 2024 BHR source; logging/support and closed-caliper retention are explicit workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Left fork: fill the damper chamber
steps.instruction: Fully extend the damper assembly. Measure and add 216 cm³ of Yamaha Suspension Oil S 1 to the damper chamber. This is the initial cartridge fill, not the outer fork fill.
verification: left: S1 initial damper fill216 cm³ recorded; damper fully extended.
steps.origin: Original illustrated companion reconciled against exact 2024 BHR source; logging/support and closed-caliper retention are explicit workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Left fork: bleed slowly with short strokes
steps.instruction: Pump the damper slowly several times to remove air, using strokes below 200 mm. Do not use 200 mm or more or a full stroke during this initial bleed: the manual warns that this draws air in. If air enters, repeat the full-extension, fill and initial-bleed sequence before continuing.
verification: left: Slow sub-200 mm bleed completed without drawing air; repeat performed if needed.
steps.origin: Original illustrated companion reconciled against exact 2024 BHR source; logging/support and closed-caliper retention are explicit workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Left fork: set cartridge oil level
steps.instruction: Fully extend the damper and measure oil level from its top as shown. Adjust to 145–148 mm, matching the other fork leg. Fully finger-tighten the rod locknut onto the damper assembly; do not remove it.
verification: left: Level145–148 mm recorded from illustrated top datum; rod locknut finger-tight.
steps.origin: Original illustrated companion reconciled against exact 2024 BHR source; logging/support and closed-caliper retention are explicit workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Left fork: seat the base valve using the source motion
steps.instruction: Load the damper rod to the maximum described by Yamaha, then install the base valve while releasing rod pressure, following the page 167 diagram. This is a manual loading/release operation, not a gas charge; do not add air or nitrogen. The source specifies no numerical force or complete rod-motion direction. Verify the damper is fully extended after seating; if not, repeat full extension, fill, bleed, level and seating before fastening.
verification: left: OEM seating motion followed; damper fully extended; no external charge.
steps.origin: Original illustrated companion reconciled against exact 2024 BHR source; logging/support and closed-caliper retention are explicit workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Left fork: secure the base valve and knob
steps.instruction: Hold the damper with cap-bolt ring wrench 90890-01501 and use cap wrench 90890-01911 to tighten the base valve to 28 N·m. Refit the adjuster knob and tighten its screw to 0.6 N·m using a tool accurate at that value.
verification: left: Base valve28 N·m; knob screw0.6 N·m recorded.
steps.origin: Original illustrated companion reconciled against exact 2024 BHR source; logging/support and closed-caliper retention are explicit workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Left fork: distribute oil and purge the excess
steps.instruction: Slowly pump the assembled damper more than ten times. Protect the rod end with a cloth as shown and fully compress the assembly to expel excess oil at the base-valve side. Drain overflow through the illustrated hole. About 10 cm³ overflow is an observation, not a dosing amount to subtract manually. Verify smooth travel; binding or rough spots require repeating the OEM fill-to-purge sequence.
verification: left: More-than-ten pumping cycles; full-compression purge; overflow drained; smooth damper motion verified.
steps.origin: Original illustrated companion reconciled against exact 2024 BHR source; logging/support and closed-caliper retention are explicit workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Left fork: install the seal and bushing stack
steps.instruction: Oil the inner tube with fork oil and protect its sharp seal-entry area with oiled vinyl film. Apply lithium-soap-based grease to dust- and oil-seal lips. Fit the new dust seal, stopper ring, new oil seal, washer and new slide metal in the PDF 168 order. The oil seal numbered face points downward. Remove the protective film after the seal passes the sharp area.
verification: left: New seal stack ordered and oriented as shown; lips protected/greased; film removed.
steps.origin: Original illustrated companion reconciled against exact 2024 BHR source; logging/support and closed-caliper retention are explicit workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Left fork: assemble and seat the bushings and seal
steps.instruction: Install new piston metal in its inner-tube groove. Slide on the outer tube. Use fork-seal driver 90890-01502 / YM-A 0948 (48) to seat the slide metal through its washer, then seat the oil seal until the stopper-ring groove is fully visible. Seat the ring completely in that groove.
verification: left: New piston/slide metal seated; oil seal seated; stopper ring fully engaged.
steps.origin: Original illustrated companion reconciled against exact 2024 BHR source; logging/support and closed-caliper retention are explicit workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Left fork: seat the scraper and dust seal
steps.instruction: Apply lithium-soap-based grease to the indicated inner-tube area and seat the new dust seal as illustrated. Slide the tubes to verify smooth movement. Binding or rough spots require correction and repetition of the tube/seal assembly checks; no separate scraper is installed.
verification: left: Dust seal seated; tube movement smooth.
steps.origin: Original illustrated companion reconciled against exact 2024 BHR source; logging/support and closed-caliper retention are explicit workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Left fork: set the locknut position and spring stack
steps.instruction: Measure from the damper-assembly bottom to the locknut bottom exactly as shown; adjust the locknut until that distance is at least 16 mm. Install the upper spring seat with its larger-diameter end facing the spring, then the spring. Lower the damper assembly slowly into the inner tube until it contacts the bottom; do not drop it.
verification: left: At least16 mm recorded; spring seat faces spring; cartridge lowered without impact.
steps.origin: Original illustrated companion reconciled against exact 2024 BHR source; logging/support and closed-caliper retention are explicit workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Left fork: fit the rod, washer and adjuster
steps.instruction: Record and fully loosen the rebound control. Compress the inner tube and position the ring wrench under the locknut as illustrated. Fit the damper adjusting rod, new copper washer and adjuster. Finger-tighten the adjuster fully onto the damper rod. Before torquing, measure the gap between adjuster and locknut: it must be 0.5–1.0 mm. Correct the locknut/adjuster position if outside that range.
verification: left: Rebound fully loosened; rod/new washer fitted; gap0.5–1.0 mm recorded.
steps.origin: Original illustrated companion reconciled against exact 2024 BHR source; logging/support and closed-caliper retention are explicit workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Left fork: tighten both adjuster joints
steps.instruction: Hold the locknut and tighten the adjuster-to-damper joint to 29 N·m. Release the supporting tool under controlled spring load. Apply the specified LOCTITE locking agent to the adjuster-to-inner-tube thread shown on page 171, then tighten that joint to 55 N·m. The OEM does not identify a LOCTITE grade or cure time here; record the actual product used and follow its application instructions without treating an invented grade as an OEM value.
verification: left: Rod joint29 N·m; inner-tube joint55 N·m; locking agent recorded; supporting tool removed.
steps.origin: Original illustrated companion reconciled against exact 2024 BHR source; logging/support and closed-caliper retention are explicit workflow adaptations.

steps.title: Left fork: fill the separate outer chamber
steps.instruction: Measure and add 270 cm³ of Yamaha Suspension Oil S 1 to the outer fork chamber. This is separate from the earlier 216 cm³ cartridge fill. Use the same standard quantity in both legs. Temporarily thread the damper assembly into the outer tube and refit the protector guide. Final top tightening follows during bike refit.
verification: left: Outer S1 fill270 cm³ recorded; damper temporarily threaded; guide fitted.
steps.origin: Original illustrated companion reconciled against exact 2024 BHR source; logging/support and closed-caliper retention are explicit workflow adaptations.

steps.instruction: With the bike securely supported on its wheels, push down on the handlebars several times and confirm smooth fork rebound before final axle-nut tightening, as Yamaha specifies.
